_**Agent (composer-2-fast)**_


Your `map` + `join` usage is fine. If an array has several items, you get several names separated by commas; `join` is not what hides them.

What usually explains “I know this project has multiple skills but I only see one (or they’re missing)” here:

### 1. The grid always uses the **second** project, not “the one you edited”

`PortfolioGrid` passes a **fixed index** into `GridItem`:

```140:140:components/public/portfolio-grid.tsx
                        <GridItem variant='project' section={section} project={projects[1]} key="c" />
```

So the card always shows `projects[1]` (0-based: the **second** row after `orderBy`). If you gave multiple skills to the first or third project, this card still shows whatever `projectSkills` the **second** project has—often a single skill.

### 2. Runtime data may only have one row

At render time, `project.projectSkills` is whatever came from `getProjects()`. If that project only has one row in `project_skills`, `join` can only produce one name. The admin table can be showing a different project or you might be assuming the wrong project is on the public grid (see above).

### 3. Layout clipping (less common for “missing names,” but possible)

The card uses `overflow-hidden` on the root `Card` in `grid-item.tsx`. The grid cell also has a fixed height from `react-grid-layout`. Very tall content can be **cut off** at the bottom, so long skill lists might be partially hidden. That’s a CSS/layout issue, not `join`.

---

**Summary:** `join` concatenates whatever strings `map` returns. If you don’t see multiple skills, either `projectSkills` doesn’t contain multiple entries for **that** `project` object, or you’re not rendering the project you think you are—right now that’s almost certainly the case because of `projects[1]`.
